proof.label: The whiteboard test — five days straight, and in a group
proof.why: A repeatable protocol, not an anecdote: someone writes a number he cannot see, he leaves the body, reads it, comes back and calls them.

proof.label: Three years trying to disprove himself
proof.why: The frame a proof reel needs — he set out to catch himself hallucinating and started targeting things he could check.

proof.label: Kelly watches her son in the military
proof.why: A second person's verified account, checked by phone straight after.

proof.label: A number on a piece of paper, verified in group settings
proof.why: The same test told tighter than D1's, and it says other people reproduced it.

proof.label: Why the CIA spent millions on remote viewing
proof.why: Institutional corroboration — a different flavour of proof from a personal anecdote.

proof.label: Eighty-four witness accounts
proof.why: The count. Ends before the speaker changes at 3:48.

proof.label: He described the tunnels under the pyramids BEFORE they were confirmed
proof.why: The strongest proof in either interview: a claim he says he made publicly, on the record, in advance — then the tunnels were found. Not a private anecdote.

heart.label: The heart is not a pump — it is an electromagnetic generator
heart.why: The thesis. The field is what glues the soul into the body; lower the field and you come out. Dying and going out on purpose are the same mechanism.

heart.label: Sleep paralysis is the doorway — delta waves and a very low heart rate
heart.why: The how-to. Panic raises the brainwave, which raises the heart rate, which raises the field, which snaps you back awake.

heart.label: Going further down until you come right out
heart.why: The last step of the method, and that he taught himself to do it at will.

heart.label: Five senses, one percent of the light spectrum
heart.why: The cleanest statement of the limit — you cannot see a radio signal, and that is the whole argument in one line.

heart.label: The soul is physical — you look at your hands
heart.why: What happens the moment you are out, and why he says it is more real, not less.

heart.label: Cats see more of the spectrum, and there is equipment that does too
heart.why: His bridge from the claim to something testable with hardware.

heart.label: The body is the computer, the field is the internet
heart.why: His own analogy for what you are reading when you read someone — the picture practically draws itself.

heart.label: Water holds memory — the rice experiment
heart.why: The most literally illustratable science-z claim in either interview: two jars, thirty days.

heart.label: The heart is a toroidal field, and the body mirrors the construct
heart.why: Ties the heart back to the shape of everything else — a diagram moment.

heart.label: An empty house rots — so does an empty body
heart.why: His argument that the soul generates the vessel, made with something everyone has seen.

heart.label: Telepathy is the same field, turned up
heart.why: Connects the heart mechanism to an ability, which is what the video is arguing.

heart.label: Zero point energy, the domes on old churches, and the balloon
heart.why: A copper wire round a balloon, a grounding rod, and you pull energy out of the air. He offers it as something you can actually do.

heart.label: Moving water makes a field — and baptism was reprogramming it
heart.why: The science-z reading of a ritual, which is exactly the register you asked for.

heart.label: Immortal genes, telomere caps and the placebo effect
heart.why: Where he reaches hardest for real biology — worth having even if it only survives as a line.

heart.label: Twelve-strand DNA and twelve structures in the brain
heart.why: The hinge between this video and the speculative one — put it in whichever it suits.

spec.label: The firmament, NASA composites, and Operation Fishbowl
spec.why: The construct as he draws it: a plane, a dome, the waters above.

spec.label: Twelve heavens, not seven — and he names the ladder
spec.why: A vertical stack of twelve, each rung labelled in his own words.

spec.label: The pyramids were machines — and airports
spec.why: A pyramid drawn as equipment: aligned to stars, wired into the ground.

spec.label: The tunnels beneath the pyramids, and the halls of Amenti
spec.why: Cutaway: the pyramid above, the deep shafts and coils below.

spec.label: Cities underneath, entrances blocked, mountains that are buried pyramids
spec.why: A grassy hill in cross-section with a pyramid inside it.

spec.label: Antarctica: the treaty, the pyramids, the bodies
spec.why: Ice with structures under it, and a treaty page full of signatures.

spec.label: Giants — including one he says was shot in Afghanistan
spec.why: Scale: a human figure against the thing he is describing.

spec.label: The mountains are tree stumps
spec.why: A flat-topped mesa with a tree's growth rings across the top. Uluru.

spec.label: Atlantis, the Mayans, dragons, and flying craft in old pictures
spec.why: A medieval painting with the craft in it circled.

spec.label: Project Looking Glass — reading time instead of predicting it
spec.why: Branching paths seen from above rather than a straight line.

spec.label: Fixed event markers, and the freedom point he says is coming
spec.why: Whatever route you take, the same point on the map.
